goal: `mc publish --body-file <path>` puts the file's text in the pull request's body, on the first publish and on an open pull request alike.
`mc merge <repo> <pr> --docs` squashes exactly the head whose file list it checked, and refuses with `drift` when the head moved.
contract: Ruling 43 (`docs/project/mc/rulings.md` § 43): every push through `mc publish`, never a force push; the squash lands the head that was checked.
`mc merge --docs` keeps every refusal it has (`read`, `state`, `draft`, `not-docs`, `script`, `empty`, `conflicting`, `merge`, `merge-unknown`) and its wording.
out_of_scope: Waiting in `--docs` for GitHub to catch up with a push that has not reached it: the head is read from GitHub, and that head is the one checked and pinned.
Other `scanArgs` callers: `mc run`'s loop flags already read both spellings.
The rest of the 2026-10-17 `mc shot` / `mc gate <files>` proposal.

success_criteria.criterion: `run(['--body-file', 'b.md'])` with `deps.read` returning `File body.` creates the pull request with body `File body.` plus the mark, and on an open pull request edits it to that body.
success_criteria.check: `node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs tests/mc/publish.test.js` passes, including the tests named in step 1.

success_criteria.criterion: `runDocsMerge` calls `gh pr merge <n> --squash --subject … --match-head-commit <headRefOid>`, and stops at `drift` without calling merge when the head read after the mergeability wait differs from the one read with the files.
success_criteria.check: `node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs tests/mc/docs-merge.test.js` passes, including the tests named in step 2.

steps.title: mc publish --body-file is read
steps.done_when: `src/mc/commands/publish.js` reads `flags['body-file']`; the two new tests in `tests/mc/publish.test.js` pass; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: on memoro-cli #939 (2026-10-17) `mc publish --body-file <path>` opened the pull request with the last commit's message as its body. `scanArgs` (`src/mc/commands/flags.js`, `key()` near line 61) keys a flag by its name without the leading `--`, so `--body-file` is `flags['body-file']`; `src/mc/commands/publish.js` lines 65–66 read `flags.bodyFile`, which is always undefined. Checked: `scanArgs(['--body-file','x'], { strictValues: ['--body-file'] }).flags` is `{ 'body-file': 'x' }`.
Fix: in `run` in `src/mc/commands/publish.js`, replace both `flags.bodyFile` with `flags['body-file']`. Nothing else in the file changes.

Tests in `tests/mc/publish.test.js`, inside `describe('mc publish', …)` next to the `--body` tests (around lines 100–125), using the same fixture those tests use, with `deps.read = (path) => (path === 'b.md' ? 'File body.' : null)` added to the deps: (1) no open pull request, `run(['--body-file', 'b.md'], deps)` returns 0 and the `pr create` call's `--body` is `'File body.

<!-- mc:described aaaaaaa1111 -->'` (use the head sha that fixture gives); (2) an open pull request #4, the same call returns 0 and the `pr edit` call is `['pr', 'edit', '4', '--body', 'File body.

<!-- mc:described aaaaaaa1111 -->']`. If the fixture builds its deps without a `read` key, add the key in the test, not in the fixture's defaults.
`mc gate tests/mc/publish.test.js`, then `mc gate`, `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`.

steps.title: mc merge --docs pins the squash to the head it checked
steps.done_when: `runDocsMerge` passes `--match-head-commit` with the head read beside the file list and stops at `drift` when the head moved; the new tests in `tests/mc/docs-merge.test.js` pass; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why (ruling 43): `runDocsMerge` in `src/mc/docs-merge.js` checks GitHub's file list (all under `docs/`, no script) and then runs `gh pr merge <n> --squash --subject …` with no pin. A push between the check and the squash lands files nobody checked — possibly code. The gate form already pins (`src/mc/repo-merge.js` around line 320).

In `runDocsMerge`: add `headRefOid` to the first `view(gh, pr, 'number,title,state,isDraft,baseRefName,files')` call's fields and keep it as `const head = info.headRefOid || null;`, and set `report.head = head`. If `head` is null, `return finish('read', `gh gave no head for #${pr}`)` right after the existing `read` refusal.

After the mergeability loop and the `CONFLICTING` refusal, read the head again: `const now = view(gh, pr, 'headRefOid')?.headRefOid || null;`. When `now !== head`: `return finish('drift', `#${pr} moved on GitHub from ${String(head).slice(0, 7)} to ${String(now || 'nothing').slice(0, 7)} after its files were checked — not merged; run mc merge --docs again`)`.

The merge call becomes `gh(['pr', 'merge', String(pr), '--squash', '--subject', `${info.title} (#${info.number})`, '--match-head-commit', head])`. The code after it (reading `state,mergeCommit` back) is unchanged: a head that moved in the last instant is refused by GitHub and reported as `merge` with gh's own line.

Comment above the second read: one or two sentences — the squash lands the head whose files were checked and no other (ruling 43), the way `repo-merge.js` pins the gate form. Add `drift` to any list of `stopped_at` values in this file's comments, if there is one.

Tests in `tests/mc/docs-merge.test.js`. Extend `stubGh` (line ~14) with two options, `head = 'aaaa111'` and `headAfter = head`: the default `pr view` answer (the one with `files`) also carries `headRefOid: head`, and a view whose fields are exactly `headRefOid` answers `{ headRefOid: headAfter }`. Every existing test keeps passing without other change. Then in `describe('runDocsMerge')`: (1) the existing 'lands a docs-only pull request…' test also asserts the `pr merge` call ends with `'--match-head-commit', 'aaaa111'`; (2) new: `stubGh({ files: ['docs/a.md'], headAfter: 'bbbb222' })` → `stopped_at` is `drift`, `ok` is false, the reason contains `aaaa111` and `bbbb222`, and no call in `calls` starts with `['pr', 'merge']`; (3) new: `stubGh({ files: ['docs/a.md'], head: null })` → `stopped_at` is `read`.
`mc gate tests/mc/docs-merge.test.js`, then `mc gate`, `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`. This is the plan's last step: in the same PR set both `success_criteria[].met` to true in this plan.
